<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Stock Options  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Options granted generally vest over four years with 25% vesting on the first year anniversary and the remainder continuing to vest
ratably every month thereafter, and expire no more than 10&nbsp;years from the date of grant. We recognize compensation cost on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period of the award. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, we granted options to employees and nonemployees to purchase 497,163, 185,400 and 922,794 shares of common stock at
a weighted-average exercise price of $19.95, $9.23 and $5.28 per share, and a weighted-average fair value on the date of grant of $10.34, $4.98 and $2.88 per share, respectively. The intrinsic value
of stock options exercised during the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012 was $7.1&nbsp;million, $3.7&nbsp;million and $0.6&nbsp;million, respectively. The 2002 Plan allows
certain holders to exercise their options prior to completion of the vesting period. In the event of termination of employment prior to completion of the vesting period, we reserve the right to
repurchase the unvested shares at the original price paid by the holder. During fiscal 2008 and 2011, employees exercised 85,786 and 54,474 options, respectively, prior to completion of the vesting
period. Cash received in exchange for the unvested shares was classified as other liabilities, the share options are not deemed exercised, and the related shares are not considered outstanding until
they become vested. As of January&nbsp;31, 2012, 15,564 restricted shares associated with the early exercise provision were outstanding. As of January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, there were no
restricted shares associated with the early exercise provision outstanding. </FONT></P>

outstanding at January&nbsp;31, 2014 have a weighted-average remaining contractual life of 7.6&nbsp;years and a weighted-average exercise price of $9.46 per share and options
exercisable have a weighted-average exercise price of $4.93 per share. As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, the aggregate intrinsic value of options outstanding was $19.1&nbsp;million,
$10.5&nbsp;million and $5.4&nbsp;million, respectively. As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, the aggregate intrinsic value of options exercisable was $12.6&nbsp;million,
$7.0&nbsp;million and $3.9&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We

calculate the fair value of the options, certain assumptions are made regarding components of the model, including risk-free interest rates, volatility, expected dividend yield, and expected option
life. The use of different </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Restricted Stock  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On July&nbsp;31, 2012 and in connection with our acquisition of Agile Advantage,&nbsp;Inc., we issued 9,600 shares of restricted
stock. All of such shares vested in full on July&nbsp;19, 2013. The fair value of approximately $0.1&nbsp;million was recorded as compensation expense over twelve months. The restricted stock was
issued from the 2002 Plan and reduced the number of shares available for grant. </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Employee Stock Purchase Plan  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The price at which common stock is purchased under the 2013 ESPP is equal to 85% of the fair market value of the common stock on the
first day of an offering period or on a purchase date, whichever is lower. The initial offering commenced on April&nbsp;11, 2013 and the initial purchase date was December&nbsp;13, 2013. During
the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;31, 2014, 158,329 shares were issued under the 2013 ESPP for an aggregate purchase price of $1.8&nbsp;million. Accumulated employee withholdings of
$0.5&nbsp;million at January&nbsp;31, 2014 associated with the next purchase date on June&nbsp;13, 2014 were included in other current liabilities. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
the fourth quarter of fiscal year ended January&nbsp;31, 2014, we completed an intercompany sale of certain intangible assets between our Finland subsidiary and us. In connection
with this sale, we incurred a $0.6&nbsp;million current tax liability in Finland. A deferred charge of $0.3&nbsp;million related to the sale is presented in other assets in accordance with the
intercompany asset sale guidance required by GAAP. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have historically incurred operating losses in the United States and, given our cumulative losses and limited history of profits, we have recorded a full valuation allowance against
our United States deferred tax assets for all periods to date. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
ability to use the operating loss carryforwards to offset future taxable income is subject to restrictions enacted in the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. These
restrictions limit the future use of the operating loss carryforwards if certain ownership changes described in the Internal Revenue Code occur. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the valuation allowance increased by $6.9&nbsp;million and $4.3&nbsp;million, respectively, due to the increase in
deferred tax assets, primarily the net operating loss and research and experimentation tax credit carryforwards. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
of January&nbsp;31, 2014, we had federal and state net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $75.3&nbsp;million and $56.5&nbsp;million, respectively. At
January&nbsp;31, 2014, we also had federal research and experimentation tax credit carryforwards of $3.7&nbsp;million. The net operating loss carryforwards and tax credits expire at various dates
through January&nbsp;31, 2034. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued) </B></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> (12) Income Taxes (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
believe that we have not taken an uncertain tax position on prior tax filings and therefore have not recorded a liability for unrecognized tax benefits. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
file federal, state, and foreign income tax returns in jurisdictions with varying statutes of limitations. With few exceptions, tax years 2001 through 2013 remain subject to
examination by federal and most state tax authorities due to our net operating loss carryforwards. In the foreign jurisdictions, the 2009 through 2013 tax years remain subject to examination. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> (13) Net Loss Per Share Attributable to Common Stockholders  </B></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We calculate basic and diluted net loss per share of common stock by dividing net loss attributed to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock
outstanding during the period. We have excluded all potentially dilutive shares, which include redeemable convertible preferred stock, warrants for redeemable convertible preferred stock and common
stock, outstanding common stock options, outstanding restricted stock units and restricted common stock, from the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding as their inclusion in
the computation for all periods would be antidilutive due to net losses. Our redeemable, convertible preferred stock and unvested common stock issued pursuant to the "early exercise" of options are
participating securities and are excluded from the earnings per share calculation as they do not have an obligation to share or fund in our net losses. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
following common stock equivalents were excluded from consideration in diluted net loss per share because they had an antidilutive impact: </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> (14) Employee Benefit Plan  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2004, we adopted the Rally Software Development Corp. 401(k) Plan (the 401(k) Plan). The 401(k) Plan is available to all full-time employees with eligibility commencing on the first
day of employment following attainment of age 21. Employees may contribute up to 90% of their eligible compensation, not to exceed the amounts allowed by law. Currently, there is no employer
contribution or matching provisions in the 401(k) Plan. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> (15) Commitments and Contingencies  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We lease office space and certain equipment under operating leases having terms that expire at various dates through May 2025. On
June&nbsp;10, 2013, we entered into an amended and restated office lease, which superseded and replaced our lease for our corporate headquarters located in Boulder, Colorado. In addition to the
office space we currently occupy, the amended and restated office lease provides for the lease by us of an additional 89,000 square feet of office space in a building to be constructed adjacent to our
current office space. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
initial term of the amended and restated office lease is ten years and will commence upon the occupancy date of the new building, currently expected to be on or about June&nbsp;1,
2015, and extend through May&nbsp;31, 2025, in each case subject to change based on the construction schedule. The lease term for the current office space has been extended to end contemporaneously
with the end of the initial term for the amended and restated office lease. We have the option to extend the term of the lease for two periods of five years each. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In

restricted cash is reflected as restricted long-term cash on our balance sheet and replaces the former security deposit, which was a $2.5&nbsp;million letter of credit that has been cancelled.

</UL>

on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows, except for those matters for which we have recorded a loss contingency. We accrue for loss contingencies when it is both probable that
we will incur the loss and when the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, there were no material pending or threatened legal actions or proceedings against us. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> (d) Self-insurance reserves  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective January&nbsp;1, 2013, we use a combination of insurance and self-insurance plans to provide for the potential liabilities
for employee medical health care benefits. Claims with dates of service prior to January&nbsp;1, 2013 were covered and paid by our prior premium-based medical insurance plan. Liabilities associated
with the risks that are retained by us are estimated by considering historical claims experience and severity factors. We have individual employee stop-loss as well as overall stop-loss coverage to
limit our total exposure. Our estimated self-insurance liability for claims incurred but not reported was approximately $0.1&nbsp;million and $0.2&nbsp;million at January&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013,
respectively, which amount was included in accrued liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> (e) Severance  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

$1.1&nbsp;million consisting of $1.0&nbsp;million in cash and $0.1&nbsp;million in stock-based compensation. As of January&nbsp;31, 2014, approximately $0.2&nbsp;million was included in
accrued liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheet. The remaining balance will be paid in the first quarter of the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;31, 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> (16) Subsequent Event  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have evaluated subsequent events that occurred after January&nbsp;31, 2014 through April&nbsp;11, 2014, the date at which the consolidated financial statements were issued. No
material events were identified. </FONT></P>
